Proactive Chinch Bug & Grub Prevention Treatment

As we transition into the summer season, conditions across our region have created an elevated risk environment for one of South Florida's most damaging turf pests, the chinch bug. Following an exceptionally harsh drought period, turf that is already under stress is particularly vulnerable as rising temperatures signal the beginning of peak chinch bug activity. Acting now, before populations establish and spread, is the most effective and cost-efficient approach to protecting your community's turf.

Juniper Landscaping is recommending a proactive application of Arena, the industry's leading systemic insecticide for chinch bug control. This treatment is specifically timed to target both adult chinch bugs and their nymphs at the optimal window in their life cycle, maximizing effectiveness and helping break the reproductive cycle before damage becomes visible.

Why Arena:

Extended Residual Control — Arena provides over 30 days of proven control, giving your turf sustained protection through the most active period of the season rather than a short-term knockdown that requires repeat treatments.

Dual-Purpose Protection — In addition to chinch bug control, this application will also provide preventative coverage against grubs, delivering two layers of protection in a single treatment.

Cycle Disruption — By targeting adults and nymphs simultaneously at this critical window, we are not simply treating what is visible today, we are reducing the population's ability to reproduce and which will help reduce the population going into the active season.

Chinch bug damage can escalate quickly in heat and drought-stressed turf, and by the time it becomes visible, significant loss has already occurred beneath the surface. This proactive approach is designed to get ahead of that curve and preserve the investment your community has made in its landscape.

Definitions of Terms (Refer to scope of work services provided under this proposal)
Thinning 
Includes crown cleaning as well as selective removal of branches to increase light penetration and air movement through the crown, and to reduce weight of certain branches.

Dead wooding
 The trimming operation will include the selective removal of water sprouts and dead, diseased, broken, or weakly attached branches from the tree.

Crown Elevation 
Branches will be removed, and growth redirected as needed to clear pedestrian and vehicular traffic areas, entrances to buildings, lights, signs and other structures, as well as providing adequate space for other trees and shrubs.

Crown Reduction 
Includes overall reduction of the crown for the purpose of reducing the size of the tree. Terminal shoots will be selected to be cut back to lateral branches.  The lateral branches will be oriented to maintain the natural shape of the tree (e.g. not growing toward the interior of the crown).  The basal diameter of the lateral must be at least 1/3 the basal diameter of the terminal at the point of removal.  The final cut in removal of a terminal branch will preserve the entire branch collar of the remaining lateral. The angle of the cut will parallel the upper angle of the remaining lateral.

Building Clearance
Branches will be removed so as to provide clearance from roofs, gutters, buildings, and carports or other structures. The objective is to provide a minimum of 4-6 feet clearance and to reduce the branches growing towards the objects requiring clearance.

Palm Pruning
Palms will be pruned to remove nuts and dead or dying low-hanging fronds.

Bed Weed Control:  
All landscape bed areas where weeds are evident will be treated with herbicide to keep these areas relatively weed free.  Large weeds will be pulled by hand so as not to be allowed to have enough established quality to detract from the overall aesthetics of the landscape.

Safety Border:

Unless otherwise agreed upon, a 6 inch safety border will be sprayed around all areas where grass grows up to a structure or building, light poles, back flow preventer, screens and other equipment or structures. This safety border is intended to prevent damage to equipment and structure. If the community does not want the safety border, Juniper Landscaping will not be held responsible for damages to these areas.

Pruning:

Shall be performed to maintain the natural shape and plant palette characteristics. Pruning shall include, but not limited to, the removal of vegetation that is dead, damaged, or diseased. When diseased vegetation is removed, the pruning cuts shall be made deep into the healthy plant tissue to re-establish healthy growth. Should flat tops and sides be desired, this will be achieved by the use of gas-powered shears. Should the association request additional trims, an additional services proposal can be provided at the time service is requested. All trimming and pruning shall be subject to all applicable State, Federal, and ANSI (American National Standards Institute) regulations. 

Arbor (Below 12 FT):

Trees: Pruned to remove any dead or damaged branches. This will include cross- branching and the raising of canopies to allow safe pedestrian movement on sidewalks and driveways in accordance to good canopy structure. Trees over 12 feet in overall height requiring service at canopies shall be performed at the Owner’s request and expense. 

Palms: Fronds shall be removed when frond tips are brown and or damaged with the clean edge cuts made as close to the trunk as possible. Careful trimming procedures shall be followed to prevent damage to any portion of the tree, especially in the crown shaft and bud area. Inflorescence or seedpods and fruit shall be removed on a set cycle. Palms over 12 feet in overall height requiring service at canopies shall be performed at Owner’s request and expense.
